documentation_ledger.why_seven_and_not_four: Two targets needed a second read: the anchor's indices schema was not on the page its own anchor points at, and one ONYPHE sentence had to be checked verbatim. Section 35 permits the minimal chain needed to reach an exact first-party document, and both extensions stayed inside a named target.

the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.$comment: The most important process fact in this mission. Recorded here rather than buried in a partner record.
the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.what_happened: The first read of the query-language page returned, in analytical prose, that the time-range functions filter on time of data collection and not on record modification dates, and that they filter by observation period rather than record state. That is precisely the distinction the temporal-object test turns on, and taking it at face value would have moved ONYPHE's B2 from PARTIAL to PASS.
the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.why_it_was_re_read: It arrived as characterisation rather than in quotation marks, unlike the timestamp definition on the data-model page, which came back quoted. Mission 1.61 re-read the anchor's lineage sentence for the same reason and the re-read CONFIRMED it.
the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.what_the_re_read_found: The page does not contain that sentence. What it contains is a section titled for time-range functions described as allowing search through historical data, and calendar-bucket boundary definitions for the hour, day, week and month functions. Nothing states what the filtered timestamp means at record level.
the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.consequence: ONYPHE B2 stays PARTIAL. A verdict that would have been recorded on a sentence that does not exist was not recorded.
the_verbatim_re_read_that_changed_a_verd.the_rule_this_confirms: A retrieval summary is not a document. Where a single sentence decides a gate, it is quoted or it is not relied on.

the_endpoint_that_was_not_executed.endpoint: the anchor's indices endpoint, documented at get /api/indices/
the_endpoint_that_was_not_executed.why_not: Section 5 permits executing a configuration endpoint only where repository evidence proves its response carries no target measurement values or records. No such evidence exists, so it fails closed. Its response might well be pure scan metadata; might is not proof.

request_accounting.the_count_is_measurement: A response naming which ports a scan configuration covered is apparatus metadata. A response carrying host records, or a number of matching service observations, is measurement. The second was never requested.
request_accounting.the_trial_is_not_free: A zero-cost trial, demo console or search preview destroys preregistration exactly as a paid one would.
